test_candidates.title: Using a proprietary compliance system
test_candidates.question: What does it mean to operate under a proprietary internal compliance system?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What does it mean to operate under a proprietary internal compliance system?
summary: Covers compliance obligations in node 1 of the paraphrase test set.

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: Our organisation operates under a proprietary compliance system developed specifically for our risk profile. This system prescribes controls, evidence standards, and escalation paths that differ from generic frameworks.

key_points: The proprietary compliance system is not publicly documented.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "Example Shipping Ltd Protocol" as "our proprietary compliance system"

test_candidates.title: Applying a seven-series control standard
test_candidates.question: How does the seven-series control standard differ from ISO 27001?
test_candidates.canonical_question: How does the seven-series control standard differ from ISO 27001?
summary: Covers compliance obligations in node 2 of the paraphrase test set.

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: The seven-series control standard specifies data-handling obligations beyond what ISO 27001 mandates. Teams must demonstrate quarterly evidence per control family.

key_points: The seven-series standard has stricter data-handling requirements than common public frameworks.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "MRD-7" as "the seven-series control standard"

test_candidates.title: Preparing for the flagship audit initiative
test_candidates.question: What special preparation does the flagship audit initiative require?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What special preparation does the flagship audit initiative require?
summary: Covers compliance obligations in node 3 of the paraphrase test set.

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: The flagship audit initiative demands pre-audit dry runs, designated evidence custodians, and a readiness scorecard submitted 30 days before the audit window opens.

key_points: The flagship audit initiative has a 30-day pre-submission requirement.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "Project Apex" as "the flagship audit initiative"

test_candidates.title: Interpreting a compliance rate in the mid-eighties
test_candidates.question: What does a compliance rate near eighty-seven percent indicate about gap exposure?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What does a compliance rate near eighty-seven percent indicate about gap exposure?
summary: Covers compliance obligations in node 4 of the paraphrase test set.

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: A compliance rate near eighty-seven percent signals material gaps in roughly one in eight controls. Organisations at this level should prioritise gap closure before the next assessment window.

key_points: A rate in the mid-eighties corresponds to roughly 13% of controls unmet.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "audit score 87" as "current compliance rate is eighty-seven percent"

test_candidates.title: Remediating a control shortfall in subsection four-point-two
test_candidates.question: What remediation steps close a control shortfall found in subsection four-point-two?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What remediation steps close a control shortfall found in subsection four-point-two?
summary: Covers compliance obligations in node 5 of the paraphrase test set.

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: A control shortfall in subsection four-point-two typically involves missing documentation of approval chains. Remediation requires retrospective documentation and a forward process change.

key_points: Subsection four-point-two shortfalls are documentation failures, not process failures.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "Section 4.2 gap" as "a control shortfall in subsection four-point-two"

test_candidates.title: Citing internal policy corpus in compliance evidence

sections.heading: Detail
sections.body_md: Internal policy documents from our organisation's policy corpus are acceptable primary evidence when the control explicitly requires policy alignment. Auditors prefer current-revision documents.

key_points: Internal policy corpus documents must be current-revision to count as evidence.

_test_meta.desc: Paraphrase of "Example Freight Co. Internal" as "our organisation's internal policy corpus"

key_points: A near-eighty-seven-percent baseline against a proprietary system requires a multi-quarter roadmap.

test_candidates.title: Carrier permit management overview
test_candidates.question: How does Example Freight Co. (fictional) track operating permits for its carrier fleet?
test_candidates.canonical_question: How does a freight carrier track operating permits for its fleet?
summary: Permit management ensures every vehicle in the fleet holds current authorisation.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Permits are logged in a central register with expiry dates. Reminders are issued 90 days before expiry and vehicles with lapsed permits are taken off-road automatically.

key_points: Automated expiry tracking prevents lapsed-permit operations.

test_candidates.title: Load documentation requirements
test_candidates.question: What paperwork must accompany every freight load at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What documentation is required for every freight load?
summary: Correct load documentation reduces delays at border and inspection points.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Every load requires a consignment note, a weight certificate, and a signed chain-of-custody form. Hazardous loads need an additional manifest. Missing documents trigger a hold before departure.

key_points: No load departs without a full documentation set.

test_candidates.title: Customs compliance in international freight
test_candidates.question: What customs obligations apply when Example Freight Co. (fictional) moves goods across borders?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What customs obligations apply to international freight movements?
summary: Accurate commodity codes and declared values are the foundation of customs compliance.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Shipments crossing a customs border require a declaration with the correct HS commodity code, declared value, and country of origin. The customs broker reviews each declaration before submission.

key_points: Incorrect commodity codes are the leading cause of customs delays.

test_candidates.title: Fleet vehicle safety inspection schedule
test_candidates.question: How often are fleet vehicles safety-inspected at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: How often should freight vehicles undergo safety inspections?
summary: Regular safety inspections prevent on-road failures and regulatory penalties.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Heavy vehicles are inspected every six months; light vehicles annually. Inspections cover brakes, lights, tyre condition, and load-securing equipment. Failed vehicles are removed from service until cleared.

key_points: Six-monthly inspections apply to all vehicles over 3.5 tonnes.

test_candidates.title: Driver qualification and certification tracking
test_candidates.question: How are driver certifications monitored at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: How should a freight company track driver qualifications?
summary: Driver qualifications must be current for every class of vehicle operated.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Each driver record includes licence class, medical clearance date, and any endorsements for specialist loads. The system flags upcoming expirations and suspends scheduling for drivers with lapsed qualifications.

key_points: Drivers with expired medical clearances cannot be assigned loads.

test_candidates.title: Incident reporting for road freight operations
test_candidates.question: What must be reported after a road incident at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What is the incident reporting requirement for freight operators?
summary: Timely incident reports protect the company and satisfy regulatory obligations.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: All on-road incidents, including near-misses, must be logged within 24 hours. Incidents involving injury or cargo loss are escalated to the safety officer and reported to the regulator within 48 hours.

key_points: Near-miss reporting is mandatory — not just injury incidents.

test_candidates.title: Temperature-controlled cargo requirements
test_candidates.question: What cold-chain controls apply to perishable freight at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What cold-chain controls apply to temperature-sensitive freight?
summary: Unbroken temperature records are essential for perishable cargo compliance.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Refrigerated loads require a calibrated temperature logger active from loading to delivery. Logs are retained for two years. Any excursion outside the agreed temperature band is reported to the consignee before delivery.

key_points: Temperature excursion records must be disclosed, not concealed.

test_candidates.title: Dangerous goods handling basics
test_candidates.question: What packaging and labelling rules apply to dangerous goods at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: What packaging and labelling rules apply to dangerous goods in freight?
summary: Correct classification and labelling of dangerous goods is a legal requirement.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Dangerous goods must be classified under the relevant ADR/IATA table, packed in UN-approved containers, and labelled with the correct hazard diamonds. Drivers must carry emergency information sheets for every dangerous goods line.

key_points: ADR/IATA classification determines packaging, labelling, and driver training requirements.

test_candidates.title: Freight billing reconciliation process
test_candidates.question: How are billing discrepancies identified and resolved at Example Freight Co. (fictional)?
test_candidates.canonical_question: How should a freight operator reconcile billing discrepancies?
summary: Accurate billing reconciliation prevents revenue leakage and customer disputes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Invoices are matched against proof-of-delivery records and fuel surcharge rates before dispatch. Discrepancies above a defined threshold are escalated to the accounts team and resolved within five business days.

key_points: Automated invoice matching catches most discrepancies before they reach the customer.

summary: Approved-provider status requires passing a financial, insurance, and safety assessment.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: New logistics partners are assessed on three dimensions: financial stability, insurance coverage levels, and safety performance history. Providers must pass all three to join the approved list. Annual re-assessment ensures ongoing compliance.

key_points: Partners must pass all three criteria — none can offset another.
